title: Mandatory Safety Barriers at Escalator Handrails
what_it_is: Mandatory Safety Barriers at Escalator Handrails

sections.label: Escalator and balustrade safety requirements
sections.summary: The Code requires balustrades designed to discourage climbing and handrails of a certain height, and the Building Control Act requires safety barriers of at least one metre at escalator landings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The Code includes several safety requirements to reduce the risk of users falling over handrails.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For instance, balustrades have to be designed to discourage users from climbing across the handrails.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Handrails also have to be of a certain height.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the Building Control Act requires safety barriers of at least  one metre at escalator landings to prevent users from falling through the gaps between two escalators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: These requirements are in line with international standards across Europe and the United States.

sections.label: Raising escalator safety awareness
sections.summary: The Building and Construction Authority is working with building owners and operators to raise public awareness on safe and proper escalator usage, such as by displaying posters on safety tips.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The Building and Construction Authority is working with building owners and operators to raise public awareness on safe and proper usage of escalators, such as by displaying posters on safety tips.

sections.label: User behaviour and lifts
sections.summary: User behaviour is a major part of escalator incidents, and buildings with escalators will likely also have lifts people can use if they feel there is a risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: User behaviour is also a major part of incidents that occur on escalators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In many buildings where there are escalators, there will also likely be lifts which people can use if they feel that there is a certain risk to them and others around them.
